quests.hint: Choosing between options and settling on one.
quests.explanation: Make a decision, make a promise and make a complaint are all fixed pairings with make, so the verb cannot help you. English chooses make or do by habit rather than logic.

quests.hint: To give plants the liquid they need.
quests.explanation: Do me a favour introduces a request, and what follows could be watering, moving or checking the plants. The verb is squeezed between and and the, where attention usually drops.
quests.textToSpeak: Could you do me a favour and water the plants?
quests.textWithBlanks: Could you do me a favour and ___ the plants?

quests.hint: An informal way of saying a very long time.
quests.explanation: It took me ages is vague and casual, while months and weeks are precise. Ages is one of the most common informal exaggerations in spoken English.
quests.textToSpeak: It took me ages to get used to the new system.
quests.textWithBlanks: It took me ___ to get used to the new system.

quests.hint: A short form meaning I would have.
quests.explanation: I'd, I've and I'll are three different short forms that all begin with the same sound and last a fraction of a second. Here I'd stands for I would, and it points to something that never actually happened.
quests.textToSpeak: I'd have called, but my phone was completely dead.
quests.textWithBlanks: ___ have called, but my phone was completely dead.

quests.hint: It was possible for you to do it, and you didn't.
quests.explanation: Could've, should've and would've are almost identical in fast speech, but they express blame, advice and imagination in turn. The 've is reduced to a tiny 'uv' sound.
quests.textToSpeak: You could've told me it was cancelled.
quests.textWithBlanks: You ___ told me it was cancelled.

quests.hint: Short for they have, about people who are not the speaker.
quests.explanation: They've, they'd and we've are all grammatically fine here, but they change who is being talked about and when. Pronoun plus auxiliary is where a huge amount of meaning hides in English.
quests.textToSpeak: They've been living there since April, I think.
quests.textWithBlanks: ___ been living there since April, I think.

quests.hint: To take an item back to the shop and get your money.
quests.explanation: Return, exchange and swap are the three things you can do with an unwanted item, and only return gets your money back. Shops treat these as different transactions, so the word matters.
quests.textToSpeak: I'd like to return this, but I've lost the receipt.
quests.textWithBlanks: I'd like to ___ this, but I've lost the receipt.

quests.instruction: Something's missing! Grab the right brick to fix the sentence.
quests.hint: Your money returned to you in full.
quests.explanation: A refund gives you money, a discount reduces a price, and a voucher keeps your money in the shop. Customer service staff use all three constantly, so the difference is worth hearing clearly.
quests.textToSpeak: We can offer you a refund or a credit note.
quests.textWithBlanks: We can offer you a ___ or a credit note.

quests.instruction: Something's missing! Grab the right brick to fix the sentence.
quests.hint: To reach you, at your door.
quests.explanation: Arrive means it reaches you, while ship and dispatch mean it merely leaves the warehouse. Companies often use the second kind of word to sound faster than they are.
quests.textToSpeak: Your order should arrive within three working days.
quests.textWithBlanks: Your order should ___ within three working days.

quests.hint: As ___ as means the moment it happens, with no delay.
quests.explanation: As soon as means immediately, as long as sets a condition, and as often as talks about frequency. The frame is identical, so the middle word does all the work.
quests.textToSpeak: I'll text you as soon as I get there.
quests.textWithBlanks: I'll text you as ___ as I get there.

quests.hint: Not open.
quests.explanation: Shut, packed and closing all give a reason to go elsewhere, so the second half of the sentence cannot help you. Shut is the everyday spoken alternative to closed.
quests.textToSpeak: The shop was shut, so we ended up going elsewhere.
quests.textWithBlanks: The shop was ___, so we ended up going elsewhere.

quests.hint: At the moment the first action is complete.
quests.explanation: Once and after both mean the form is finished first, but before reverses the whole order of events. Instructions live or die on these small linking words.
quests.textToSpeak: Once you've filled in the form, hand it to reception.
quests.textWithBlanks: ___ you've filled in the form, hand it to reception.

quests.hint: Packages being sent or delivered.
quests.explanation: Drop off means deliver something and leave it, and parcels, forms or samples could all be dropped off. Drop off these runs together, so the noun comes fast.
quests.textToSpeak: I need to drop off these parcels before five.
quests.textWithBlanks: I need to drop off these ___ before five.

quests.hint: This particle means reducing gradually, not stopping completely.
quests.explanation: Cut down on and cut back on both mean reduce, while cut out means stop entirely. Three real phrases, one tiny word of difference, and a completely different level of commitment.
quests.textToSpeak: I'm cutting down on caffeine this month.
quests.textWithBlanks: I'm cutting ___ on caffeine this month.

quests.hint: Arrived, often unexpectedly or without warning.
quests.explanation: Turned up and showed up both mean arrived, while got up means left bed. All three are followed by up, so the verb in front is the only clue.
quests.textToSpeak: She turned up half an hour late without apologising.
quests.textWithBlanks: She ___ up half an hour late without apologising.

quests.hint: A place where you sit down and are served a meal.
quests.explanation: Shall we say seven is a natural way of proposing a time, and the meeting place could be anything. Restaurant, theatre and gallery all carry their stress on the first syllable.
quests.textToSpeak: Shall we say seven, outside the restaurant?
quests.textWithBlanks: Shall we say seven, outside the ___?

quests.hint: To send a short written message from your phone.
quests.explanation: Text me, call me and ring me are three equally normal requests, and all three are single short syllables at the very start of the sentence. Openings are hard to catch because you are still tuning in.
quests.textToSpeak: Text me when you're on your way and I'll come down.
quests.textWithBlanks: ___ me when you're on your way and I'll come down.

quests.hint: Already organised, with nothing left to worry about.
quests.explanation: It's all sorted, covered and arranged mean much the same in a friendly context, so meaning alone cannot separate them. Sorted is the most casual of the three in British speech.
quests.textToSpeak: Don't worry about bringing anything, it's all sorted.
quests.textWithBlanks: Don't worry about bringing anything, it's all ___.

quests.hint: The number of days in this new working week.
quests.explanation: Four, three and five are all believable new working weeks, so only the number itself, not the sentence, tells you the answer. After a long phrase, the final number is easy to lose.
quests.textToSpeak: I've cut my hours down to four days a week.
quests.textWithBlanks: I've cut my hours down to ___ days a week.

quests.hint: Moving fast on foot, as exercise.
quests.explanation: Take up means start a new hobby, and running, swimming or painting would all clear someone's head. All three end in -ing, so the difference is at the start.
quests.textToSpeak: He's taken up running to clear his head.
quests.textWithBlanks: He's taken up ___ to clear his head.

quests.hint: Become calm and stable again.
quests.explanation: Settled down, calmed down and quietened down all describe life becoming easier, and all three take down. The verb is unstressed in the middle of the sentence.
quests.textToSpeak: Things have settled down a lot since the move.
quests.textWithBlanks: Things have ___ down a lot since the move.

quests.hint: At any time up to now, in a question expecting news.
quests.explanation: Yet, before and recently all sit comfortably at the end of this question but carry different expectations. Yet suggests the speaker thinks you probably haven't been.
quests.textToSpeak: Have you been to the new place on the corner yet?
quests.textWithBlanks: Have you been to the new place on the corner ___?

quests.hint: To succeed in doing something difficult.
quests.explanation: Did you manage to, did you forget to and did you remember to are three real questions with opposite assumptions behind them. Get hold of someone means reach them by phone.

quests.hint: Expected to, because that was the arrangement.
quests.explanation: Supposed to, meant to and due to all express an expectation that has not been met, and all three are natural here. Supposed to is usually pronounced 'spose-tuh' with no z sound at all.
quests.textToSpeak: Wasn't he supposed to be here by now?
quests.textWithBlanks: Wasn't he ___ to be here by now?

quests.hint: The date by which work must be finished.
quests.explanation: Push something back means delay it, and a deadline, a handover or a review could all be pushed back. Deadline is a compound with stress on the first part: DEAD-line.
quests.textToSpeak: Can we push the deadline back to Friday?
quests.textWithBlanks: Can we push the ___ back to Friday?

quests.explanation: Chasing up means pursuing something that is overdue, while checking and sending describe calmer actions. It is a very common word in British workplaces.

quests.hint: In meetings, this means setting a topic aside for later.
quests.explanation: Park that, leave that and hold that all mean postpone the discussion, and all three are heard in meetings. Park has nothing to do with cars here, which is why context matters.

quests.textWithBlanks: Let's ___ that for now and come back to it next week.

quests.hint: To make your details appear on the screen.
quests.explanation: Bring up, pull up and look up an account are all things call handlers say while you wait. Bear with me is the polite way of asking for a few seconds of patience.

quests.textWithBlanks: Bear with me a second while I ___ up your account.

quests.hint: Waiting on the line while the other person does something.
quests.explanation: Put you on hold, on speaker and on mute are three different things that can happen to your call. Only hold means you have to wait.
